name: Rethinking Attention with Performers
problem: Attention is O(n^2) in time and memory. To go linear one must approximate the softmax kernel, but existing approximations either assume sparsity or low-rankness - priors that rarely hold for attention - and their accuracy was never checked at real scale.
mechanism: FAVOR+ (Fast Attention Via positive Orthogonal Random features): the softmax kernel is approximated by a positive random-feature map of a randomised orthogonal matrix, making the attention matrix an unbiased estimator of the true softmax attention. Unbiasedness, uniform convergence and low estimation variance are all proved. The approximation needs NO sparsity or low-rankness assumption, which is the specific gap the paper closes.
speedup_reported: NOT A THROUGHPUT CLAIM, and this is the honest reading of the abstract. Performer's claims are about EXPRESSIVITY and comparability: 'we demonstrate competitive results with other examined efficient sparse and dense attention methods' across pixel-prediction, text and protein-sequence tasks, plus the theoretical guarantees. The abstract does attach a number to one capability - protein language-model code and the Google AI blog are referenced - but no linear-vs-quadratic wall-clock multiple with a named baseline and hardware appears. Any specific Performers speedup figure in circulation comes from the blog post, not this paper.
